subject: Satellite VPC on-prem integration: control & data plane alignment
messages:
From: Claire Benson <claire@edgeworks.io>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@atlascloud.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Satellite VPC on-prem integration: control & data plane alignment

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the quick sync yesterday. EdgeWorks is starting prep for the first satellite site (SE-chi-01) and we want to lock the control-plane <-> data-plane handoff and the egress rules before we push the staging nodes.

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm control-plane endpoints (FQDNs + TLS trust model) for the on-prem connector. We prefer mTLS but can accept token-based auth for initial pilot.
- Data-plane outbound egress: we have strict allow-listing; need a short list of IP ranges and ports.
- Service discovery: how will the runtime (inference nodes) reach the model registry and KV cache (control-plane)? Will DNS be private with split-horizon or will we rely on host routes?

I attached a topology snapshot (satellite-vpc-topology-v1.pdf) and a link to our internal runbook. Can you share Redwood's reference control-plane diagram and any ops playbook you'd like us to adopt?

Target: staging cutover on 2026-11-02, we'd like to freeze config by 2026-10-25.

Thanks,
Claire Benson
Head of Integrations
EdgeWorks Inc.

Attachments: satellite-vpc-topology-v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Claire Benson <claire@edgeworks.io>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@atlascloud.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Satellite VPC on-prem integration: control & data plane alignment

Claire — thanks for the topology and timeline. Looping in Irene (network/security lead) and Naomi (ops) from our side; Kimberly is our private-deploy PM so she can track the config freeze.

Quick responses and what we'll provide by EOD Friday (2026-10-22):
- Control-plane endpoints: canonical FQDNs and a short TLS spec (we support mTLS; token fallback for initial pilot). I attached our reference diagram (redwood-controlplane-ref.svg).
- Egress list: Samir, can you confirm Atlas's side for whitelisting? If Atlas supplies the upstream IP set, we'll mark ports (443, 5222 for internal RPC, 9411 for tracing endpoint optional).
- Service discovery: recommended pattern is split-horizon DNS for private hosts with internal DNS entries pointing at the local edge relay; host routes only as fallback. We'll include a small migration guide for host-route fallbacks.

Open questions for you:
1) Do you need HSM/KMS integration from our side or will EdgeWorks manage key material locally and exchange certs?
2) Any specific egress inspection (TLS termination / SNI rewrite) policies we need to be aware of?

Action items (from Redwood):
- Deliver control-plane FQDNs + cert exchange steps (2026-10-20)
- Provide ops-handoff checklist and runbook fragment (ops-handoff-checklist.md) (2026-10-22)

I'll attach the reference diagram.

— Mateo
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-controlplane-ref.svg (svg)
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Claire Benson <claire@edgeworks.io>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Satellite VPC on-prem integration: control & data plane alignment

Thanks — a few clarifying points from security/network:

mTLS and certs
- We prefer mTLS for the control plane. Claire, can EdgeWorks generate server certs for the local relay and accept Redwood client certs? If you need us to push certs into your fabric, we can use an automated CSR flow (s2a-like) or manual exchange for the pilot.
- If local KMS is planned, we need the KMS endpoint and whether it is reachable over the same VPC peering/subnet or via a proxy.

Egress and IP allowlist
- Please provide the minimal set of IP CIDRs that must be permitted for control-plane management and model fetch. We will try to collapse RTP (real-time protocol) ports behind the relay.

Observability & audit
- For SOC2 evidence: we need to ensure audit logs for model loads, config rollouts, and operator API calls are forwarded to a central location (S3/GCS or syslog). Naomi — will Redwood accept a signed log bundle or do you need a push to our forwarding endpoint?

Failover/latency constraints
- For the satellite site, expected RTT to Redwood control-plane (us-east) is ~60–80ms. That drives our cache TTL for KV and prefix cache. We'll propose TTL=10s for heavy inference workloads; let us know if you need tighter.

I'll draft a small matrix of decisions and post to the shared drive.

Irene Choi
Network & Security Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@atlascloud.com>
To: Claire Benson <claire@edgeworks.io>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: ECS Ops Team <ecs-ops@atlascloud.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Satellite VPC on-prem integration: control & data plane alignment

Hi all — quick from Atlas (ECS) side on egress and discovery:
- Attaching the egress CIDR dump (atlas-egress-ranges.csv). For the pilot, the minimum required outbound CIDRs are the two /22 blocks listed in the first sheet; allow TCP 443 and TCP 9411 (optional tracing).
- DNS: we recommend split-horizon. We can publish internal A records into your on-prem zone via a delegated view. If you prefer, we can also provide host-route artifacts (BGP community tags) for the edge router.
- Ports: model fetches use 443; runtime RPC uses 5222 on the private mesh but the relay collapses this to a single outbound port when NAT'd.

I'll follow up with a signed statement for compliance if needed.

— Samir
AtlasCloud ECS — Integrations

Attachments: atlas-egress-ranges.csv (csv)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Claire Benson <claire@edgeworks.io>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, ECS Ops Team <ecs-ops@atlascloud.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Satellite VPC on-prem integration: control & data plane alignment — ops handoff checklist and next steps

Team — summary and next steps from ops readiness perspective. We validated the topology and have a short acceptance checklist for the pilot cutover on 2026-11-02.

Acceptance checklist (pilot):
1) Control-plane cert exchange complete (mutual TLS configured) — status: pending (mateo to send cert bundle 2026-10-20).
2) Egress allow-list applied at EdgeWorks perimeter (two Atlas /22 CIDRs + port 443 allowed) — status: Samir to confirm; expected completion 2026-10-21.
3) Split-horizon DNS or host-route fallback in place — status: Claire to confirm DNS view by 2026-10-22.
4) Observability forwarding configured: system logs and model-load audit exported to Redwood S3 staging bucket or supplied as signed bundle — status: open (Irene/Claire to agree).
5) Runbook & rollback: ops-handoff-checklist.md uploaded to Confluence and shared with on-call rotation; rollback steps validated in dry-run — status: Naomi to run dry-run on 2026-10-28.

Deliverables Redwood will attach to the ticket (AT-9876):
- control-plane FQDNs + cert exchange instructions (redwood-controlplane-ref.svg + cert-exchange.md)
- ops-handoff-checklist.md (attached)
- documented TTL recommendations (TTL=10s default; can tighten to 5s with caveat re: RTT)

Claire — can you confirm the DNS plan and KMS approach by Friday 2026-10-22 so we can lock the config? If EdgeWorks wants Redwood to host the KMS proxy for the pilot, we can scope that as an optional task but it will add a small integration window.

Thanks everyone — we feel ready to proceed once certs and egress are confirmed.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: ops-handoff-checklist.md (md)
